question: What four main areas of a temporary traffic control zone are shown in Figure 6B-1, in order of travel?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Figure 6B-1 shows a TTC zone divided into four areas which, in the direction of travel, are: (1) the advance warning area, (2) the transition area, (3) the activity area, and (4) the termination area. This division is described as informational (Support) — a TTC zone is "often divided into four areas as needed, based on engineering judgment," not as a mandatory layout. Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 6B-1 depicts the four areas in travel order (bottom to top): the Advance Warning Area "tells traffic what to expect ahead," the Transition Area "moves traffic out of its normal path" (with shoulder taper and channelizing devices), the Activity Area "is where work takes place" (containing the work space, traffic space, and buffer spaces), and the Termination Area "lets traffic resume normal operations" (with the downstream taper). [Image 2] Page 813 reproduces the same Figure 6B-1 layout with identical labeling of the four areas. [Image 3] Page 812 contains Section 6B.03, stating the four areas are the advance warning area, transition area, activity area, and termination area, illustrated in Figure 6B-1. [Image 4] Page 1033 (Section 8A.13) addresses TTC zones at grade crossings and does not add to the four-area description. [Image 5] Page 811 (Section 6B.02) defines TTC zones generally but does not enumerate the four areas. Citations: - Section 6B.03 Support §1 (p.771) - Figure 6B-1 (p.772) - Page 813 - Page 812
gold_answer: Advance warning area, transition area, activity area, and termination area.
